"I would treat antepartum haemorrhage as an obstetric emergency and first assess maternal stability using an ABCDE approach. I would call for senior obstetric and anaesthetic assistance, establish two large-bore IV accesses if significant bleeding is present, send FBC, group and crossmatch, coagulation including fibrinogen where indicated, and renal function, and activate the major obstetric haemorrhage protocol if required. I would assess fetal wellbeing with CTG when appropriate and ultrasound, including placental location. I would specifically avoid digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia has been excluded. I would consider placenta praevia, placental abruption, vasa praevia and uterine rupture, using the history and examination to guide the differential. I would administer blood products and correct coagulopathy as required, consider anti-D in an eligible RhD-negative woman and corticosteroids if preterm delivery is anticipated. Finally, I would determine the safest timing and mode of delivery based on the cause, gestation, maternal condition and fetal status."
